retro:
# Retrospective

## Worked

Fresh native Opus 5.5 High and Sol Xhigh sessions were verified, including Opus response model metadata. Managed Team 4 identity was checked before reset. Both reports stayed unread until both independent finals existed. Read-only triage covered directly linked issues and correctly treated audio crash/recovery reproductions as ordinary bug context, not malicious intent. Source-only Sol and synthetic Opus approaches supplied complementary evidence; no native hardware claims were manufactured. Editorial used only exact draft and immutable privacy-inclusive requirements and passed freshly.

## Process deviations and correction

1. Sol read eight native session JSONL lines, but a large line overflowed the tool cap and automatically persisted native session metadata/assignment prompt outside the assignment. Preserve history. Identity checks should parse only session/model/thinking records or first three records and print minimal fields, not dump verbose lines.
2. Opus did not fully read the coordinator corrections before experiments, and truncated some security paragraphs. Requested complete remaining bounded reads without per-line truncation. A read range is not complete if byte/line caps cut it.
3. Opus fixture inventory listed output classes and guarded parent OUT, but not every final target. Core-limit status, case receipt/summary redirections, command substitution and fail-immediate semantics did not meet instructions. Original report overclaimed final-target guards. Preserve original and add audit correction. Coordinator independently read fixture and all raw child results; narrow successful synthetic paths remain usable alongside independent source evidence. No suite-wide safety compliance claim.

Assignment-local corrective checklist for any future runtime work: literal each-callee/final-target/producer inventory, assert target before writing (including stderr/status/summary/core files), gate core setter and readback separately, gate every command substitution, explicitly return failure on mismatch and gate callers immediately. These requirements already exist in coordinator workflow and were sent before work; the implementation audit remains necessary. No additional experiment is justified solely to create a compliant broad count when source settles the public findings.

## Limitations and tooling

No confirmed Omadev/tool bug or desktop slot needed. No native user manager/audio/hardware access. Long policy text imposes read overhead, but does not permit skipping corrections. External packaging snapshots should ideally be commit-pinned when they materially establish absence; this public finding remains conditional and uses inspected migration/systemd mechanics. No claim of ongoing monitoring after coordinator completion.
comment:
Two conditional paths can prevent the promised speaker-lock warning at `9d07e446f846`.

## Offline migration leaves the watcher outside the unit search path

The [failed-enable fallback](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/9d07e446f846a4ec5df33e43ca5c8ec813767838/migrations/1790123774.sh#L23-L28) creates only a `graphical-session.target.wants/` symlink to the unit under `$OMARCHY_PATH/default/systemd/user/`. That directory is outside systemd's normal user-unit search path. A successful `systemctl --user enable /absolute/path` also creates the top-level unit link; this fallback does not.

Source-derived path, not a live systemd reproduction:

```text
Update without a reachable user manager
  -> enable fails
  -> .wants link created, but no loadable top-level unit
Next graphical login
  -> target wants the watcher by name, but cannot find its unit
```

**Impact:** On an existing install taking this fallback, the watcher does not start unless the unit is separately installed in a search directory. The migration can still finish, leaving no speaker-lock warning. The system-service restart override is independent of this issue.

**Suggested change:** Also create the top-level linked unit in the user unit directory, checking both link operations, or package the service under `/usr/lib/systemd/user` and enable it by name.

## Failed notification readiness consumes the only warning

[`announce_lock`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/9d07e446f846a4ec5df33e43ca5c8ec813767838/bin/omarchy-audio-speakersafetyd-watch#L42-L68) returns success when `omarchy-notification-wait` times out. The caller then unconditionally sets `notified=1`.

```text
Two locked polls -> readiness times out -> notified=1, no toast
Lock persists    -> notification server returns -> no retry
```

**Impact:** A delayed notification server at startup or during a shell restart can suppress the warning for the entire continuous lock episode. A synthetic locked-state sequence confirmed one readiness attempt and no send or later retry; the server-recovery consequence follows from the unchanged `notified` state.

**Suggested change:** Return failure when readiness or sending fails, and set `notified=1` only after successful delivery. Handle failure conditionally so the watcher continues polling rather than exiting under `set -e`.

**Verified:** The watcher only reads mixer controls. With synthetic lock and notification responses, it warns once for a sustained lock, suppresses alternating locked/unlocked observations, and warns again after unlock/relock. The focused PR shell test passed. Source inspection confirms the drop-in disables the start limit and sets five-second restart spacing.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned-source review and isolated shell tests with stubbed audio, timing and notification calls. No native Asahi hardware, 96 kHz crash/recovery, live systemd activation or real notification delivery was tested. Offline unit resolution is source/documentation-derived.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium initial inspection and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical reviews, and a fresh Astra Medium editorial check. Public claims were checked against source and retained targeted evidence.
